mc.q: A bus company provides an online service for passengers to find bus routes. What information should passengers input?
mc.exp: To find a route the system only needs where you start and where you go; stops and fare are outputs.

mc.q: What are the 8-bit one's complement and 8-bit two's complement of the binary number 10110₂ ?
Which of the following actions involve converting data between digital and analog forms?
mc.exp: Playing music is D→A, recording video is A→D; copying a file stays digital.

mc.q: Peter configures the colour quality of a display unit. Which of the following pixels are involved?
mc.exp: Display pixels are made of red, green and blue sub-pixels (RGB).

mc.q: Peter and Mary share a database file X and execute database queries, T1 and T2, respectively. Which of the following activities should the database management system not do?
st: (1) When T1 is reading X, T2 is reading X.
(2) When T1 is writing records in X, T2 is writing records in X.
(3) When T1 is deleting records in X, T2 is reading X.
mc.exp: Simultaneous reads are safe; any write/delete while another accesses X can cause inconsistent data, so it must be locked.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about clicking a hyperlink in a presentation file is correct?
o: The hyperlink needs to involve HTTP.
A browser will not open when the hyperlink is “http://hkeaa.edu.hk/abc.doc”.
A PDF reader will usually open when the hyperlink links to a PDF file.
The presentation file will close automatically when the hyperlink links to another presentation file.
mc.exp: The OS opens a linked file with its associated program, e.g. a PDF reader for .pdf.

mc.q: What formatting feature is used in the spreadsheet below?
mc.exp: Before: one long line in a cell; after: text broken onto several lines inside the same cell = wrap text.

mc.q: Mr Chan wants to produce a list of students who get 80 marks or above in a test, as shown in the spreadsheet below. Which functions should he use?
mc.exp: Filter keeps only marks ≥ 80; the result list is in descending order, so it is also sorted.

mc.q: Assume that every household has a residential telephone number. In which of the following database applications could the residential telephone number be used as a key field?
mc.exp: A Towngas account is one per household, so the household phone number is unique; people in one home share it.

mc.q: Why should a software suite be used in an IT project?
st: (1) Data used in the project can be shared within the software suite effectively.
(2) Data files generated by the software suite are smaller.
(3) The project will be in a web-based format.
mc.exp: Programs in a suite share data and a common interface easily; file size and web format are not guaranteed.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about a check digit for a data item is correct?
o: The data item should not contain more than 8 characters.
The check digit cannot find all errors.
The check digit can correct errors.
The leading character of the data item should be a letter.
mc.exp: A check digit detects many (not all) errors and cannot correct them.

mc.q: When editing a document, which of the following word processing features can enhance its readability?
mc.exp: Tables and footnotes change how the reader sees the content; find and replace is an editing tool.

mc.q: When using presentation software, the view mode is changed from single-slide to multiple-slide. What is/are the potential benefit(s) of this change?
st: (1) It is easier to insert an image.
(2) It is easier to re-arrange slides.
(3) It is easier to see an overview of the slides.
mc.exp: Slide-sorter view shows all slides, good for overview and reordering, not for editing content.

mc.q: Which of the following is the main development trend for display units in desktop computers?
mc.exp: Monitors moved from CRT to LCD/LED mainly to save energy (and space).

mc.q: Tom currently uses a software package on a desktop computer. He tries to install this software on his tablet computer but fails. Why?
st: (1) The tablet computer uses a different operating system.
(2) The tablet computer uses a virtual keyboard.
(3) The tablet computer uses a solid-state drive.
mc.exp: Software is built for a particular OS/platform; keyboard and drive type do not stop installation.

mc.q: Why do many readers like using mobile devices to read books?
st: (1) The ergonomic design of mobile devices helps relieve eye strain.
(2) Mobile devices provide various functions which make reading convenient.
(3) It is convenient for carrying a lot of books.
mc.exp: Search, bookmarks, many books in one device are real benefits; screens do not relieve eye strain.

mc.q: Carey wants to upgrade the DDR II 2G 667 MHz RAM of her computer to DDR III 2G 1333MHz RAM with a higher data transfer rate. Which of the following features should be considered?
mc.exp: DDR3 needs a motherboard with DDR3 slots/chipset support.

mc.q: What is the main purpose of having a memory cache in a CPU?
o: It increases the total memory storage capacity.
It supports multi-core processors on the motherboard.
mc.exp: Cache holds frequently used data close to the CPU, so processing is faster.

mc.q: When buying a wireless broadband router for a network at home, which of the following considerations is not necessary?
o: The data transfer rate of the broadband connection
The IP address of the router
mc.exp: The router's IP address can be configured anytime; it is not a buying consideration.

mc.q:
Carol uses a digital camera to take photos of her school hall. The photos will be uploaded and shown on the school's web pages.
Which of the following image file types are suitable for her to use?
mc.exp: Photos for the web: PNG and JPG support many colours and browsers; GIF has only 256 colours, TIFF is too big/not web.

mc.q:
Carol uses a digital camera to take photos of her school hall. The photos will be uploaded and shown on the school's web pages.
Before uploading a photo, what should Carol do?
o: If the file size of the photo is very large, she should divide it into small files for uploading.
She should reduce the photo size to fit the display.
She should adjust the resolution of the photo so that it is as high as possible.
She should adjust the number of colours shown in the photo to the highest number possible.
mc.exp: Resize the image to the display size to cut file size and load time.

mc.q:
Henry lives in Hong Kong. He likes bags made in Europe so he buys a bag through the online shopping web site of a shop in France.
What are the possible reasons for Henry's choice to buy the bag online?
st: (1) He can select and buy the bag during office hours in France.
(2) There are many different kinds of bags for Henry to choose from.
(3) The bag is not for sale in Hong Kong.
(4) He has a credit card to pay for it.
mc.exp: Online shops are open 24 h, so office hours don't matter; having a card is a means, not a reason.

mc.q:
Henry lives in Hong Kong. He likes bags made in Europe so he buys a bag through the online shopping web site of a shop in France.
There are different kinds of online shopping web sites. What features do they usually have?
mc.exp: Shops need payment (EFT) and a DBMS for products/orders; p2p and mainframes are not typical.

mc.q: Which of the following can enhance the security of online banking?
mc.exp: Security tokens add a second authentication factor.

mc.q: Why should network interface cards (NICs) be used in a computer network?
st: (1) The network needs to support data transfer at 10GB per second.
(2) NICs connect computers to the network.
(3) NICs convert analog signals into digital signals and vice versa.
mc.exp: A NIC is the hardware that connects a computer to the network; A/D conversion is a modem's job.

mc.q: When using Internet search engines, it is better to include operators like ‘+’ in search strings because
o: the search time can be shorter.
the search results include the titles of web pages only.
the search results can be more relevant.
the search results can include both local and foreign web sites.
mc.exp: Operators narrow the search, so results are more relevant.

mc.q: At home, Mary cannot access the HKEAA's web site by entering http://www.hkeaa.edu.hk, but she can do it by entering http://210.0.205.228. Why?
o: The DNS server is out of service.
The web server is out of service.
Her web browser needs an extra plug-in.
The router used at home is out of order.
mc.exp: The IP works, so only domain-name resolution (DNS) fails.

mc.q: John can view an online video on the computer at home but not on the computer in his school. Why?
o: The operating system does not support the video playback.
The browser does not support the video playback.
The video is not in HTML format.
The maximum data transfer rate of the school network is low.
mc.exp: The school browser may lack the needed plug-in/codec support for the video.

mc.q: In an IT project, Tom has written the source code. He tests it with valid input data items. What should he do next?
o: Check the modularity of the program design.
Continue to test the program with invalid data items.
mc.exp: Testing should cover invalid (and boundary) data too, before documentation.

mc.q: When P = Q and Q = R, what is the output?
mc.exp: P > R? No → Q > R? No → output 'Z'.

mc.q: If the three input values are different, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The output is ‘X’ if P is the largest value.
The output is ‘X’ if P is the smallest value.
mc.exp: X is output only when P > R and P > Q, i.e. P is the largest.

mc.q:
Dry run the following algorithm on the array AR.
cnt ← 1
ind ← 1
while cnt < 100
   cnt ← cnt + 2
   AR[ind] ← cnt
   ind ← ind + 1
What is the value of AR[5]?
Which of the following statements about open source software is correct?
o: It is free of program bugs.
It can be modified and distributed freely.
It runs faster in a networked operating system.
mc.exp: Open source licences let anyone modify and redistribute the code.

mc.q:
Tom wants to store some weather information obtained from the Hong Kong Observatory. A sample of the weather information is shown below.
Temperature: 25.8
UV index: 4
Air pollution: moderate
Which of the following sets of data types is most appropriate?
o: Temperature: String, UV index: Character, Air pollution: String
Temperature: Integer, UV index: Character, Air pollution: Boolean
Temperature: Real, UV index: Integer, Air pollution: String
Temperature: Real, UV index: String, Air pollution: Boolean
mc.exp: 25.8 is real, 4 is integer, 'moderate' is text (string).

mc.q:
Andrew creates the following group message through a social networking site.

Dear best friends,
The ABC shop has raised its prices and they are so high. I am so angry!
Let's burn down the shop at midnight. Join us!
Andrew

Betty receives and forwards this message to invite her friends, but she does not join the event. Carol receives and reads this message from Betty. Carol does not take any action.
Who has/have misused the social networking site and caused damage to the society?
mc.exp: Andrew wrote it and Betty spread it; Carol only read it.

mc.q: At home, John unintentionally detects his neighbour's WiFi network without any security measures. He can fully control the wireless router. What should he do?
o: Connect to the network for web browsing only.
Connect to the network for transferring large files only.
Configure the wireless router with an authentication key.
mc.exp: Using or changing someone else's network without permission is wrong; just ignore it.

mc.q: Some teenagers in Hong Kong are addicted to playing online games. Which of the following behaviours are common in this group of teenagers?
st: (1) They prefer playing online games to joining face-to-face social activities.
(2) They play online games as a way of escaping from daily life problems.
(3) They feel irritable when being stopped from using computers.
mc.exp: All three are typical signs of Internet/game addiction.

mc.q: When a virus is spread through a Bluetooth connection, which of the following applications installed on a notebook computer can prevent the infection?
mc.exp: A firewall can block unauthorised incoming connections; email clients and browsers don't.

mc.q: The Hong Kong Government launched the Internet Support Learning Programme in 2011. The Programme helps needy students to acquire computer equipment and Internet access services. What issue is the Government addressing?
mc.exp: Helping poor students get computers/Internet narrows the digital divide.

mc.q: In a museum, visitors can stand in front of a kiosk with a monitor and a keyboard to access visitor information. Which of the following relate to ergonomic matters?
st: (1) The viewing angle of the monitor is adjustable.
(2) The height of the keyboard tray is adjustable.
mc.exp: Adjustable screen angle and keyboard height fit users' bodies; adding a mouse isn't ergonomic.

lq.stem:
Peter buys two computers with the following specifications.
TypeNotebook ComputerTablet Computer
CPU2.80 GHz1 GHz
Main memory2 GB512 MB
Storage device capacity500 GB64 GB
Display13.3" LCD9.7" LED
Input deviceKeyboardVirtual keyboard
WiFiYesYes
LAN portYesNo
USB portYesYes
Operating systemLinux (Fedora)Android

parts.q:
Name the storage devices commonly used in the two computers.
Notebook computer: ____
Tablet computer: ____
parts.ms:
Notebook computer: hard disk
Tablet computer: flash memory / SSD

parts.q:
Use Part (a) and the specifications above to justify the following arguments.
The tablet computer has longer battery operating time.
parts.ms: The CPU / storage device / display unit consumes less electricity.

parts.q: The tablet computer needs a shorter startup time.
parts.ms: The operating system (Android) / storage device (flash memory) supports the shorter startup time. / The tablet computer has fewer peripheral devices to load up and thus its startup time is shorter.

parts.q: The tablet computer is not suited to typing for a long period of time.
parts.ms: Peter cannot keep his eyes / neck / hands in a good ergonomic position. / small keyboard

parts.q: Peter wants to connect a printer to the tablet computer. Suggest two types of connectivity and describe the benefits of each.
parts.ms:
USB: The printer has a higher data transfer rate / better data security / less interference (stable).
Wi-Fi: The printer is more portable.

parts.q:
Peter takes some photos and shares them with his friends through the Internet. The protocols, HTTP, IMAP, FTP and SMTP, are used by the servers, as shown in the diagram below. [Diagram: Peter's computer —(i)→ File server —(ii)→ Web server; Web server —(iii)/(iv)→ his friends' computers; Peter's computer —(v)→ Email server —(vi)→ his friends' computers]
Fill in the protocols used for the data transmission between the computers.
(i) ___ (ii) ___ (iii) ___ (iv) ___ (v) ___ (vi) ___
parts.ms:
(i) FTP
(ii) FTP
(iii) HTTP
(iv) HTTP
(v) SMTP
(vi) IMAP
(Check the exact arrow positions on the page image.)

lq.stem: Janice opens an account on an online shopping web site and provides her personal email address and contact number. She purchases shoes through the web site. The web site uses a public and private key encryption system and owns a public key and a private key.

parts.q:
Describe how the following help to keep Janice's account secure when she shops online.
The login session is terminated automatically if the session is idle for five minutes.
parts.ms: Minimise the chance that the others use the account when the system is unattended.

parts.q: The Secure Socket Layer (SSL) is used.
parts.ms: The data are encrypted. / The identity of the web site can be validated. (trust)

parts.q: When the web site sends data with sensitive information to Janice, how will the public and private keys be used?
parts.ms: The company encrypts the data with its private key and Janice decrypts with the company's public key. / The company encrypts the data with Janice's public key and Janice decrypts with her private key.

parts.q:
Janice has forgotten the password of her account. The web site can send Janice an email with a link to activate her account and an SMS (Short Message Service) message containing a one-time password which is valid for only one login.
Give two advantages of this arrangement in terms of security.
parts.ms:
Any two (1×2):
• The two levels of authentication processes (email & SMS) can enhance the security of password reset.
• Email / SMS can authenticate Janice's identity.
• The one-time password can force Janice to use another password to avoid the damage of the leak of the password generated by the system.
(explanation of SMS / one-time password ✗)

parts.q: Janice understands that she should not use public computers to do the online transactions. Why not? Give two reasons.
parts.ms:
Any two (1×2):
• Someone might peek at her to steal her username and password.
• Her private information like username and password might be stored in the computer (e.g. cookies).
• The security of the public computers is not guaranteed because spyware (keylogger, virus, etc.) might exist.
(The security is low. / She may forget to log out the system. ✗)

parts.q:
Janice takes some photos and posts them on a social networking web site. The photos are openly accessed by Internet users. She feels shock when browsing the shopping web site because she can see her photos there.
The shopping web site has posted her photos. Explain briefly why this is an unlawful action.
parts.ms:
Janice owns the copyright of the photos.
The company should acquire Janice's permission for the right to use. / The company should pay for the use of the photos.

parts.q: Janice's friends on the social networking web site post the photos to their non-commercial web sites. Is this appropriate? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: No, her friends still need to ask for Janice's permission because non-commercial use of copyrighted works cannot be exempted.

lq.stem:
Consider the following algorithm.
A ← 1
B ← 1
While B < 20 do
   A ← A + B
   B ← A - B
   Output B

parts.q: Dry run the algorithm and write down the first three outputs.
parts.ms:
1, 2, 3
Suggested answer: (A,B) = (2,1) → output 1; (3,2) → output 2; (5,3) → output 3.

parts.q:
The algorithm is rewritten so that the number of outputs of B is stored in N. Complete the algorithm below.
A ← 1
B ← 1
N ← [____]
While B < 20 do
   A ← A + B
   B ← A - B
   N ← [____]
   Output B
Output N
Write down the final values of B and N.
Suppose the initial values of A and B are changed. The values of A and B after ‘Output B’ is executed for the first time are 9 and 4 respectively. What are the initial values of A and B?

The algorithm is implemented in a computer in which all memory addresses and data are 8-bit. The statement A ← A + B is represented by the assembly instruction ADD 1000 0000, 1000 0001 where the contents of A and B are stored in the memory addresses 1000 0000 and 1000 0001 respectively. Suppose that the initial values in the memory addresses are:
Memory addressValueDecimal Value
1000 00000000 101111
1000 00011000 0011131
Suppose that the instruction is executed once. Write down the value stored in the following: (1) Memory address 1000 0000 (2) Memory address register (MAR) (3) Memory data register (MDR)
How many different values can be represented by the memory addresses in the computer?

lq.stem:
Sarah is a teaching assistant in a secondary school. She creates a table, STUD, to store the examination scores of all the students in a database.
STUD
Field nameDescription
REGNORegistration number
CLASSClass
CNOClass number
ENAMEEnglish name
CNAMEChinese name
CHIChinese language score
ENGEnglish language score
MATHMathematics score

parts.q: Should Sarah use CNO as the key field of STUD? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: No, it is because CNO cannot be unique.

parts.q: Sarah decides to use Unicode for CNAME, instead of GB code or Big-5 code. Give a reason to support her decision.
parts.ms: It supports both traditional and simplified Chinese characters.

parts.q:
Sarah executes a SQL command on STUD with four records, as shown below. SELECT REGNO FROM STUD WHERE CLASS = '2A' and ENG > 50

What is the output?

Sarah imports the entire table into a spreadsheet for further processing. The table is shown below.

Columns A–J (row 1 = headings):

201010021A21Chan Tai Man陳大文705030

Sarah wants to use column I to store the average scores of the three subjects. She enters a formula into I2 and then copies it into the other cells. Write the formula in I2.
parts.ms: =AVERAGE(F2:H2)

parts.q:
Sarah enters the following formula into J2 and then copies it into the other cells in column J.
=IF(I2<80,IF(I2<60,IF(I2<40,"D","C"),"B"),"A")
What are the values in J2 and J3?

Sarah uses a word processor to type a report. Then she uses the spell checker to check the English words.
Give examples to explain why the following mistakes can still occur.
(1) A word which has been wrongly typed is undetected.
(2) A correct word is indicated as a wrongly spelled word.
parts.ms:
(1) The mistyped word can be found in the dictionary of the word processor. For example, ‘from’ is wrongly typed as ‘form’.
(2) The word is not in the dictionary. For example, Chinese name ‘Chan’ is typed. [Example of names, scientific terms, or spelling in UK and US]

parts.q: Other than spell checker, suggest another function of a word processor that is applicable to English words but not Chinese characters.
parts.ms: grammar check / hyphenation / thesaurus / capital letters

lq.stem: A school wants to issue electronic newsletters to replace its paper-based school newsletters so that students can use their tablet computers to download and read them. The electronic newsletters will include multimedia information. Mr Li is responsible for the publication.

parts.q: What are the benefits to students of this digitisation? Give two examples.
parts.ms:
Any two (1×2):
• The newsletters are more attractive (multimedia elements).
• Students can read a number of newsletters with ease.
• Students can search specific topics with ease.

parts.q:
Students can submit writing in electronic form and multimedia files for publication in the e-newsletter.
Students use HTML format for submission. Give two reasons to support the use of this format.
parts.ms:
Any two (1×2):
• The newsletters can be opened by browsers in different tablet computers. (portability/popularity)
• Students can use many simple tools to create their work. (development tools)
• It supports hyperlinks.

parts.q: Mr Li encourages students to submit audio files in wav format rather than other common formats. Why?
parts.ms: It contains much information of the original data so that Mr Li can edit and extract necessary audio information. (quality)

parts.q: Students submit video files in avi format, but Mr Li cannot play some of them on his computer. Why not?
parts.ms: Some students adopt some uncommon codec that Mr Li has not installed for his video player.

parts.q:
Mr Li has completed a prototype of the e-newsletter and his colleague is going to present it to the Principal and school teachers. Mr Li can prepare either a presentation file or a video demonstration for his colleague to use for the presentation. Give two benefits of each mode.
Presentation file:
Video demonstration:
parts.ms:
Presentation file (any two, 1×2):
• Work flow (timeline) can be controlled dynamically. (interactive)
• The preparation time can be shorter.
• The editing work is simpler.
• Hard copies can be provided for reference.
Video demonstration (any two, 1×2):
• The presentation is more vivid and authentic. (more visual effects)
• The pace of the presentation can be controlled by Mr Li in advance.
• It is easy for Mr Li's colleague to use.
